traits.flowering_months.note: iNaturalist research-grade records on GBIF in the south and central Puget Sound lowlands (46.7 to 48.0° N, 122.0 to 123.1° W; counted 2026-10-14): 219 records annotated as flowering (Jan 1, Feb 10, Mar 52, Apr 145, May 11); stated as the months holding at least a tenth of them, March and April. The Seed Manual (Mahonia chapter, printed p. 708, as M. aquifolium) gives March to May at 685 m in Jackson County, Oregon.

traits.fruiting_months.note: USA National Phenology Network observations (Nature's Notebook) at lowland sites west of the Cascades in Washington and Oregon (below 300 m, west of 121.8° W; 2009 to 2026, fetched 2026-10-14): 20 plant-years at 5 sites seen with ripe fruit, by the months they were seen in (Apr 2, May 3, Jun 3, Jul 13, Aug 9, Sep 7, Oct 3, Nov 1, Dec 1); stated as the months with at least a third as many as the busiest, July to September. The Seed Manual (Mahonia chapter, printed p. 708, as M. aquifolium) gives late July to early August at 975 m in Mineral County, Montana, and September and October at 685 m in Jackson County, Oregon.

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944), as Mahonia Aquifolium: stems erect, 8 dm to 20 dm (0.8 m to 2 m) high, sometimes dwarfed.

appearance.organs.bloom.season.flower_lo.note: Jepson's Manual (1925), Berberidaceae: sepals 6, in 2 circles; petals 6, in 2 circles; stamens as many and opposite them. So six petals, three and three.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Berberis aquifolium (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.69 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 1 record in 1 source); trunks 0.69, branches 0.67. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: an upright evergreen shrub with glossy pinnate leaves of spiny, holly-like leaflets and dense clusters of bright yellow flowers at the stem tips. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 1.6 m tall at 12 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: glossy dark green leaflets; yellow flower clusters; grey-tan stems. Fruit (plant roadmap P4), as in mid-July: grape-like racemes of berries, green turning powdery blue. Its year (appearance.organs.bloom.season) takes its days of bud, flower, fruit, ripe and fall from the months it flowers and fruits in, by the rules at the flowering plants (development, 2026-10-14); until then they were authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands: yellow racemes in March to May; berries blue with a bloom in July and August. The forest's packages show day 196 (mid-July) until the phenology of plant roadmap P5 sets the day from the date and the local climate.

taxon.note: Common name (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

generator.program.note: Its order's woody program (growth plan G2.3a): Berberis spans two forms and Berberidaceae's own program grows its herbs, so the species names the order's.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

taxon.scientific_name.note: WCVP v16's accepted name for the plant the spec's authors wrote as Mahonia aquifolium, which WCVP treats as a synonym.

taxon.genus.note: The genus WCVP v16's accepted name is written in.

appearance.organs.bloom.season.flower_lo.note: Its flowers drawn one by one (spec rework L1b): bright yellow cup-shaped flowers about 8 to 12 mm across, six petals within nine petal-like sepals, in dense racemes that open from the base up. From general descriptions of the species (OregonFlora, the Flora of North America and nursery and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read). The size is the flower's width, or a closed corolla's length, over the fruit's length, roughly as in life. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): six yellow petals and six sepals by hand (floras give both in two whorls of three, and three outer bracteoles), six stamens and one pistil, from the characters of Berberidaceae by the rules at the flowering plants.

appearance.organs.bloom.season.opening.note: Days from the first flower of a cluster opening to its last: a third of the days from its first flower to its first fruit as they were set by hand before 2026-10-14, a convention (no source gives a raceme's opening time).
